en: In the Sanskrit language: *Ārya-mañjuśrī-nāma-saṃgīti*. In the Chinese language:
*The Sutra of Chanting the Holy Mañjuśrī’s True Name* (聖妙吉祥真實名經).
*The Sutra of Chanting the Holy Mañjuśrī’s True Name*.

Translated by the former lecturer on the Sūtras, Vinaya, and Abhidharma, and practitioner of the Secret Mantra, the Tibetan translator Nye ba’i sde, the Śramaṇa Shi Zhi. Homage to Mañjuśrī, who possesses the form of a youth.

Furthermore, the auspicious Vajradhara, The supreme tamer among those difficult to tame, The heroic one who transcends the triple world, The sovereign, the most excellent within the secrets of the Vajra.
His eyes are like white lotuses, wondrously handsome; his face is perfectly round like a lotus flower.
With his own hands he holds a supreme vajra, which he repeatedly raises aloft and hurls.
Furthermore, he manifests successively wrathful and other forms, as well as infinite Vajradharas.
Valiantly subduing those who are difficult to tame, possessing a majestic and terrifying form,
emitting supreme light from the vajra tip, he hurls it upward with his own hand.
Endowed with great compassion and wisdom, his skillful means for benefiting beings are most excellent.
Possessing a mind of joy, bliss, and tranquility, he manifests the form of wrath;
supreme among those who practice the conduct of perfect enlightenment,
all gather before him with bodies bowed in reverence toward that Tathāgata Mahevaṃ, having paid homage to the ultimate perfect awakening.
With palms joined in reverence before him, sitting upright with right mindfulness, he made this declaration:
"O Lord of All, grant me benefit;
out of your compassion for me, may I attain the ultimate perfection within the Net of Illusion and truly realize Bodhi."
There are various afflictions that disturb his mind; Yet he does not sink or drown within the mire.

For the sake of benefiting all classes of sentient beings, To cause them to attain the unsurpassed fruit, The Bhagavān of Ultimate Perfect Enlightenment— He is the Teacher of sentient beings and their Guide.
He who has realized the supreme nature of the great *mahāmantra* and understands the excellence of the faculties and the mind—
he is the wisdom-body of the Bhagavān, the Great Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, the Lord of Speech,
and he is also the wisdom-body that has emerged from itself, Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva.
Recite that supreme *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which is of profound meaning,
vast meaning, incomparable great meaning, and most gentle; it is well-expounded as excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle,
and excellent in the end by the Buddhas of the past, and shall likewise be expounded in the future.
Now, having attained ultimate, perfect enlightenment,
and having repeatedly proclaimed it throughout the Great Net of Illusory Manifestation Root Tantra, I, the Holder of the Great Vajra,
shall now speak with melodious voice, in accordance with the commands of those infinite Buddhas who hold secret mantras.
O Bhagavān, Perfectly Awakened One and Equal One, May you grant that I may truly accomplish the dhāraṇī;
Until I have certainly emerged [from saṃsāra], I shall diligently and firmly uphold it.
May I leave no afflictions remaining And abandon all erroneous understandings.
With a mind free from distinction or difference, for the sake of all sentient beings,
he requested the Secret Lord Vajradhara to proclaim [the teachings].
Having finished speaking these words before the Tathāgata and joining his palms in reverence, he sat respectfully before him.
Furthermore, Śākyamuni Bhagavān, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Honored One among two-legged beings,
extends his preeminent tongue from his own face, broad and long,
spanning across and unfolding it so as to manifest within the threefold world-system, thereby subduing the four Māras and all hostile enemies.
Sentient beings all possess the three evil destinies; To manifest for them a pure, smiling countenance,
Within that pure Brahma-voice, Having pervaded the threefold world,
The Great Powerful Vajra-holder, Guhyeśvara, replied and spoke:
You who are fully endowed with great compassion, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, you are Mañjuśrī, the embodiment of perfect wisdom. Reciting this *Tattvanāma* brings great benefit;
it is capable of purifying and eliminating sinful karma. Listen attentively as I explain it with diligence.
Excellent, O Auspicious Vajradhara! O Vajrapāṇi, you are excellent.
For this purpose, O Lord of Secrets, I shall explain it for you with skillful artifice;
you should now listen with one-pointed attention. "So be it, Mahevaṃ! Excellent!"
Furthermore, Śākyamuni Bhagavān, the great lineage of all secret mantras,
the lineage of upholders of secret mantras and vidyās— having caused those three lineages to observe the nature of both the mundane and the supramundane—
he manifested as the great mundane lineage.
The supreme and vast seed of Mahāmudrā, The Great Seed, the Great Topknot—thus one should contemplate.
The primary verse of the words: The King of Mantras, possessing six aspects, Shall be revealed as non-dual;
The unarisen Dharma itself proclaims it.

A Ā (long) Hūṃ Ī E O Ṛ Ū LṚ LṜ A Haḥ Khaṃ A Si Ti Cchili Ma Ni Ra Na Mo La Mu Ta Ma Tra Tu Pra Ti Ma Oṃ Maṇidhara Kṣaṇadā Kṣepaṇa Pramuṣitāṅga Ma Ni Ka Ya Va Vyāhāra Arapacanā Dhyāna Mā. [The following are fourteen verses.]
The maṇḍala of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment appears.
Thus, the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Ultimate Perfectly Awakened One—*A* emerged from *A*, the supreme among all syllables;
this is the subtle syllable of great benefit.
The non-arising that emerges from within all objects is itself the cause most excellent among all teachings, for it is free from verbal expression.
This great offering that makes manifest all verbal expressions is the Great Desire, which brings joy to all sentient beings.
The great offering is great anger; it is the vast enemy of all afflictions.
The great offering is great delusion; it is the mind of folly that eliminates folly.
The great offering is great wrath; it is the very adversary of resentment and malice.
The great offering is great desire; all desires are completely severed.
Great desire is itself great bliss; great bliss is great joy and contentment.
It is the great object of form and the vast body—the great form together with the great image.
The Great Illumination and the Great Vastness; The Great Center is that which extensively upholds the vessel of vast wisdom.
The Hook of Afflictions, the Great and Central Excellence, Universally Renowned, Wondrous Hearing—all are vast.
Manifestation within the center is itself the great manifestation.
The Liberated One who grasps the great illusion, Who accomplishes benefit within the great illusion;
Who rejoices with joy within the great illusion, And performs magical feats within the great illusion;
The most honored among great donors, And the most excellent among those who uphold the great precepts.
Firmly established in great patience, Completely relinquishing through great diligence,
Abiding in meditative concentration through great dhyāna, Sustaining the body through great wisdom,
Possessing great power and great skillful means, The great vows and supreme knowledge are like a vast ocean.
The nature of great loving-kindness is immeasurable and boundless; It is also great compassion and supreme wisdom.
Possessing great wisdom and endowed with great knowledge, Great understanding is itself the great skillful means.
Endowed with great supernormal powers and great strength, Great strength as well as great swiftness.
Furthermore, you possess great supernormal powers and great renown; with great strength, you cause others to be subdued.
You are able to utterly destroy the great mountains of the three realms of existence.
Holding the great, firm, and great vajra, you are the Great Taut, the Great Hero, and the Valiant One, who bestows fear upon those in the midst of great terror.
The Venerable Mahābhūta is supreme; the Guru’s Secret Mantra is most supremely excellent.
Abiding within the characteristics of that Great Vehicle, it is the most excellent among the characteristics of the Great Vehicle.
These are the twenty-four verses and three lines below.
Because he appears within the central circle of the lords of all luminosity, one praises the one hundred and eight names of the pure *dharmadhātu*.
O Great Perfectly Awakened One, Lord of All Luminosity!
You who possess great silence, you who are the great silence, you cause [all] to appear within the great secret mantra; therein lies the principle of the self-nature of the great secret mantra.
Desiring to attain the ten perfections (*pāramitā*), one abides within those ten perfections;
these ten perfections are pure. This is the principle of the ten perfections, O Noble One, who possesses mastery over the ten stages (*bhūmi*); you abide within those ten stages.
Possessing the knowledge of the tenfold self-nature, He who upholds the tenfold purity,
the meaning within the meanings of the tenfold aspects of meaning, The Sovereign of Silence and the Lord of the Ten Powers,
who brings about every benefit without exception, Is endowed with the ten kinds of great mastery.
Free from that stainless master of conceptual proliferation,
the King of the naturally pure *tathatā* speaks words of truth without concealment; acting in accordance with what he has spoken,
he teaches non-duality within the state of non-duality, abiding in the ultimate limit of reality.
The Lion Without Self, possessing a majestic voice, whom the wild beasts of the non-Buddhists fear most intensely;
you who traverse all realms of existence with purpose, as swift as the mind of a Tathāgata;
supreme and most excellent among those who conquer the enemy, you bestow great power upon the wheel-turning monarchs.
Master of concentration, supreme in concentration, king of assemblies, lord of assemblies, sovereign of assemblies;
you who uphold and protect with great efficacy; you who possess great purpose and do not accept the kindness of others;
king of phrases, lord of phrases, master of eloquence; sovereign of phrases, infinite in phrases.
Speaking the truth with words of truth, you who proclaim the Four Noble Truths are one who does not return even among those who do not return (*anāgāmin*).
Among those taught to variously and decisively transcend like *pratyekabuddhas* and *svayambhūs*, you are the singular cause among all great beings.
The bhikṣu who is an arhat has exhausted the outflows; having subdued the sense faculties and abandoned desire, he has attained peace and fearlessness.
He has perfected the state of coolness and is free from turbidity, possessing clear understanding and supernormal powers—the Sugata of the world, supreme in his clear understanding.
Without grasping at a self or grasping at "mine," abiding in the principle of the two truths,
you have reached the far shore of saṃsāra; having completed what was to be done, you abide in the open air,
manifesting within a single gnosis, and with the vessel of wisdom, you shatter all things.
The Dharma King, in whom the sublime Dharma is perfectly manifested, shines with supreme brilliance throughout the world.

Sovereign by means of the Dharma, King among those who possess the Dharma, he can expound the wondrous path and proclaim it so that its meaning is fulfilled and his vows are accomplished; he has abandoned all falsehoods.
The inexhaustible dharma-realm is truly free from delusion; The supreme and wondrous dharma-realm is utterly inexhaustible.
Possessing the great field of merit and the excellence of abundant blessings, It possesses the vast and sublime wisdom within wisdom.
Those who possess wisdom understand existence and non-existence, And thus accumulate [merit] within the state of non-duality.
The supreme meditative concentration among all views of eternalism; Vowing to cultivate dhyāna is the self-liberation of the King of Wisdom.
Each and every one is immovable; The Most Supreme Victor possesses the three bodies and is fully endowed with the nature of the five bodies of perfect awakening.
The Universal Lord is the self-nature of the five kinds of wisdom.
Crowned with the head-ornament of the fivefold awakened nature, Holding the five eyes and free from attachment,
you cause all the Perfectly Awakened Ones to flourish. O Son of the Buddhas, supreme and subtle,
born from the source of transcendent wisdom, You appear within the Dharma, having transcended the three realms of existence.
The solitary, steadfast vajra-nature, having arisen at the very beginning as the Lord of Sentient Beings,
emerges spontaneously within emptiness; with supreme wisdom and sublime gnosis like a great fire,
it illuminates everywhere with vast radiance, making all manifest through the light of primordial wisdom.
He is the lamp for sentient beings and the torch of wisdom; possessing great majesty, he manifests radiant light.
He is the sovereign of supreme spells and the king of vidyā-mantras; as the king of secret mantras, he brings great benefit.
Possessing a great uṣṇīṣa and a rare crown, the Lord of Great Space speaks of various things.
This supreme self-nature of all the Perfectly Awakened Ones, Possessing the eye that brings joy to sentient beings,
Able to cause various marks to increase— May all the Great Sages offer worship and praise;
May they uphold the three kinds of secret mantras, And may those who hold the great *mahā-vākya* uphold the secret mantras.
In order to protect the Triple Gem, the Venerable One has proclaimed this supreme mantra of the Three Vehicles—the true and most excellent *pāśa* (lasso) possessing profound meaning.
This is the great *vajrapāśa*, the great *vajra-aṅkuśa-pāśa* held by the Great Vajradhara. These are the ten verses that follow.
This is the central enclosure (*maṇḍala*) of Akṣobhya Buddha;
therefore, the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom (*ādarśajñāna*) is praised through seventy-one names and numbers.
Vajrabhairava, the Bestower of Fear, The Vajra King with six faces and terrifying [appearance].
Six eyes and six arms, endowed with strength; likewise possessing the skeletal form and baring fangs, he who is *hala hala* and possesses a hundred faces.
He is the King of Hells, the Sovereign of Māras, the powerful Vajra who can inspire terror.
His name is Vajra, the Heart of Vajra.
The Great-Bellied Vajra-illusionist, the Lord of Vajras born from within the Vajra,
whose vajra-mind is like space; immovable, adorned with a single lock of hair,
wearing a garment of elephant-hide, he roars the great *hiṃ* and *ha ha*.
The sound of *hī hī* can strike terror;
if he laughs, there is the resonant laugh, the Vajra-laughter, the great roar of joy.
O Vajra-hero, O Great hero, Vajra-king, Great bliss! O Vajra-firm one, Great delight!
Vajra-hūṃ: the sound hūṃ roars; holding a vajra-arrow and a vajra-sword within his hand, he cuts them away until nothing remains.
All who hold vajra-instruments are of one kind with the vajra;
the vajra can repel the enemy. The blazing vajra casts forth an evil eye.
Vajra hair blazing like a flame, The Vajra has arrived, the Great Arrival;
Possessing a hundred eyes, the Vajra-eye, With vajra-hair covering his entire body.
The one with vajra-hair is solitary and peerless; His fingernails grow long and sharp as vajras.
With a vajra-heart and firm skin, holding a vajra and adorned with hair-locks of auspiciousness;
adorned with a vajra-garland, laughing with the sound "ha ha" and roaring with certainty;
possessing the six-syllable vajra-voice, with a voice of great gentleness and a great resonance.
With a unique voice throughout the three worlds, his roar resounds across the entire realm of space;
among all existing sounds, this is supreme. (The following forty-two verses:)
Appearing within the central enclosure of Amitāyus Buddha,
he praises the wondrous discerning wisdom (pratyavekṣaṇājñāna) in two hundred and seventy-five names.
True selflessness and true nature— this is the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), which is without words.
Proclaiming emptiness, you are the most excellent among the assembly;
with a roar of profound and vast sound, you are the conch shell of great resonance.
You are also the *ghanṭā* with its mighty voice, and the nature of non-abiding parinirvāṇa; throughout the ten directions, you are the great drum of the Dharma.
Formless yet most subtle among those with form, possessing various marks born of the mind;
he who manifests all marks reveals auspiciousness.
Holding the reflected image without remainder, he of unsurpassed great renown is the Great Sovereign within the three realms.
Abiding in the most supreme Noble Path, the Dharma-banner amidst great prosperity,
the sole youth within the three worlds; the Elder, the Venerable Lord of the four births,
adorned with the thirty-two marks, beloved by the three realms and exquisite therein.
He is the Knower of the World, the Supreme Teacher;
The Victorious Teacher of the world, fearless, the Honored One who rescues the world with a mind free from partiality.
The Savior among saviors, unsurpassed, he fully enjoys all things unto the very limits of emptiness; An ocean of wisdom within the understanding of all.
He who has shattered the eggshell of all ignorance, And can destroy the net of the three realms of existence;
Who extinguishes all afflictions without remainder, And reaches the great shore beyond saṃsāra—
To that one adorned with the crown of supreme wisdom-empowerment, The ultimate reality, I offer this ornament.
He extinguishes the three kinds of suffering and affliction; by extinguishing the three poisons, he attains the three liberations.
He is definitively liberated from all obstacles and difficulties, abiding in equanimity like space, transcending all stains of affliction.
He is able to understand the three times and requires no teacher.
Among all sentient beings, you are the Great Honored One; among the sashes of merit, you are the garland-sash.
Among all embodied beings, you are the supreme liberator;
in the path of space, you truly abide as the wish-fulfilling great jewel. Among all jewels, you are the sovereign lord.
Perfection is the great wish-fulfilling tree; the supreme, wondrous, pure flask, the most excellent among the great, acts for the benefit of sentient beings.
Acting in accordance with sentient beings to bring them benefit, he also understands good and evil as well as the proper times.
The Universal Lord understands omens and possesses the words of prophecy.
He understands the times and the faculties of sentient beings; he is able to bring about the three doors of liberation and is endowed with all virtues.
He understands virtue, praises the Dharma, and manifests auspiciousness—the most auspicious among the auspicious. His name is Auspicious, his renown is Excellent.
The great feast of the Dharma within the Great Cessation; The great music of great joy, complete with all respectful service;

He whose nature is auspicious with supreme renown and delight, who possesses the excellence of supreme giving—this Venerable One, The subtle and wondrous refuge, worthy of being sought as a protector.
Supreme among the supreme within the world’s enemies, free from all fear without exception;
with a crown protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*) and a crest (*śikhā*) each divided into five points; his hair is smooth and pressed flat as he wears a head-ornament;
possessing five faces, he has five topknots, and upon each of these five topknots he ties a flowered hair-band.
She is the shaven-headed one of great exertion, who practices the pure brahmacarya with supreme diligence;
she is the great ascetic who has established her practice of austerity.
She is the subtle and pure Gopikā, a brahmin who understands pure brahmacarya; at the time of transcending to parinirvāṇa, she attained pure brahmacarya.
Freed from fetters, the body is liberated; liberation and parinirvāṇa are true parinirvāṇa.
Transcending sorrow, one extinguishes sorrow; subtle, certain, and close to renunciation, one reaches the limit where suffering and pleasure are removed, transcending within the body of desire.
Incomparable and beyond all measure, it is neither seen, nor manifest, nor luminous;
yet its nature remains unchanging and it is all-pervasive. Subtle, untainted, and free from the seeds of existence, it is without dust;
being free from dust, it is stainless. It is devoid of loss, abandonment, and the faults of negligence.
The ultimate nature of sleep and awakening is self-arisen; all understanding and all clarity are the subtle and wondrous consciousness-mind.
Transcending the nature of phenomena, upholding the principle is non-dual wisdom;
for those free from delusion, it is accomplished in silence. Thus one cultivates the practices of the Perfectly Awakened Ones throughout the three times.
The Perfectly Awakened One is stainless and boundless; The primordial awakening is likewise without cause.
Possessing the unique eye of wisdom, free from all defilement, He whose body is perfect wisdom is the Tathāgata.
Through mastery over words, he proclaims extensively, Expounding the Dharma of the Supreme Great Being, the King of Men.
Proclaiming and setting forth the subtle, wondrous, and supreme state;
expounding the Lion-like One who is peerless in sublime observation and supreme joy;
a mass of majestic power, an auspicious sign within the blazing light that enters the mind; his arms radiate brilliance, making all things manifest.
The sublime great physician is the Venerable One; He who can eliminate the piercing pain is unsurpassed.
He is also the medicinal tree with flourishing branches, The great adversary that counteracts all diseases.
Supreme within the three realms that enter the mind, The auspicious one who dwells amidst the circle of excellence.
Throughout all the realms of space in the ten directions, you raise the banner of Dharma, most subtle and wondrous;

you travel as the sole, vast parasol. You are the one who possesses the compassion of the sublime mandala, the Lord of the Auspicious Lotus Dance, the Great Jewel Parasol of the Sovereign of Vast Boundaries.
Possessing the great majestic power of perfect enlightenment, He upholds the bodies of all perfectly enlightened ones.
This is the great cultivation of all perfectly enlightened ones;
This is the mark of the consecration of the great jewel of the True Dharma of all perfectly enlightened ones. The nature of all great jewels is itself sovereignty.
The nature of all phenomena, the sovereign of the world;
The Vajra-holder, the king of all, the great mind of all the perfectly awakened ones;
All the perfectly awakened ones are within the heart, the great body of all the perfectly awakened ones, And also the speech of all the perfectly awakened ones.
The Vajra Day is the Great Radiance; the Vajra Moon is the Stainless Light.
Among those free from desire and the like, he is the Great Desire.
With various colors and blazing rays of light, the Perfectly Awakened One sits in the vajra-paryaṅka posture, upholding the ultimate reality of the True Dharma.
The auspicious and perfectly awakened Padmasambhava, Who also upholds the treasury of perfect awakening,
And further holds the various kings of emanations; The vast, perfectly awakened vidyādhara-mantra,
The wise Vajra, who is the Great Sword, The truly pure and supreme syllable.
This Great Vehicle removes all suffering and affliction;
The Vajra Dharma is the vast vessel, the profound Vajra *jina-jina*. Through the wisdom of the Vajra, one understands the meaning;
All perfections (*pāramitās*) are brought to ultimate completion, And one is fully adorned throughout all the stages (*bhūmis*).
The true, pure, and selfless Dharma; the supreme light of the moon of true wisdom;
the vast and great net of illusory emanations; the sovereign of all supreme tantras;
the one seated upon the vajra, who possesses all without exception; you who uphold the body of all primordial wisdom.
All supreme and wondrous wisdom is held within the ground of the mind;
it is the great mind of all perfectly awakened ones that moves back and forth.
Furthermore, it holds the various wheels of transformation, which is the supreme nature of all essences, and it also holds the self-nature of all essences.
The various meanings of the dharma of non-arising, In a single instant of vast wisdom that sustains the intrinsic nature of all phenomena,
One understands and sustains all dharmas without exception,
manifesting the comprehension of all phenomena; This is the supreme sustenance of the silent reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Supreme, immovable, and pure by nature, Holding the wondrous bodhi of perfect enlightenment, All perfect buddhas appear before me;
The fire of wisdom blazes with intense, radiant light.
(The following twenty-four verses.)
This praises the Wisdom of Equality.
Thus, it is the manifestation of Ratnasambhava Buddha; within this central enclosure are one hundred and four names and numbers.
Accomplishing the subtle meaning according to one's aspirations, all evil destinies are completely purified.
Supreme and most excellent among all sentient beings, you who liberate all beings from their enemies, the afflictions;
alone heroic amidst the host of foes, possessing fierce power that shatters the enemy of ignorance;
adorned with the body of auspicious wisdom, you who manifest the formidable aspect of firm resolve.
She can cause a hundred hands to move; within the posture of her stride, she performs a dance.
All one hundred auspicious hands are perfectly complete as she causes a dance throughout the entire realm of space.
Upon a single portion of the earth’s central enclosure, she firmly treads with the heel of one foot.
With the divisions within his toenails, he completely subdues the pure Brahma-worlds;

this is the meaning of the Dharma of non-duality and oneness. It is the meaning of the subtle and wondrous, the meaning of fearlessness, and the meaning of the various consciousnesses endowed with form.
Within the mind, intellect, and consciousness, it possesses continuity.
His essential nature is joy beyond measure; he possesses the sublime wisdom that cherishes the nature of emptiness.
Having abandoned the craving for the three realms of existence, he brings great joy to those within them.
His form is as pure and bright as white clouds, and his radiance is as magnificent as the autumn moon.
Also like the wondrous solar disc just risen, his fingernails are like polished red copper, radiant and pure;
his crown is exquisite with a pointed tip of azure, and his sublime hair is likewise deep blue-black.
Possessing the auspicious light of great jewels, he is adorned with the ornaments of the emanation body of the Perfectly Awakened One.
He causes all hundreds of worlds to tremble, Possessing the power of the divine feet (*ṛddhipāda*), Upholding the vast and true nature of mindfulness.
Within the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), he is the king of meditative concentrations (*dhyānarāja*);
With the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) as his flowers and fragrance— He is the ocean of the Tathāgata’s virtues.
Because he understands the meaning and principles of the eightfold path, he is one who understands the true path of perfect awakening.
Toward all sentient beings, he is largely free from attachment; like space, he is without attachment, yet he arises within the minds of all sentient beings with a swiftness as if possessing a mind.
He understands the faculties and meanings of all sentient beings, and is able to seize their various minds;
he also understands the true nature of the five aggregates.
He purifies the five aggregates so that they may be upheld, decisively transcending all extremes, and is likewise able to emerge from within that very certainty.
Abiding in the path toward certain deliverance,
you proclaim the definitive emergence from all existence by uprooting the twelve links of dependent origination;
you uphold the pure twelve aspects possessing the characteristics of the meaning of the Four Noble Truths, and you understand and maintain the eightfold consciousnesses.
The twelve real meanings are brought to fulfillment; the sixteen real natures manifest as the realization of the body.

Through twenty aspects, one achieves enlightenment: the supreme resolve for all the characteristics of perfect awakening, and the illusory emanation bodies of all perfectly awakened ones, which cause them to appear throughout infinite billions of realms.
He clearly understands those various moments,
as well as the diverse meanings of all moments and the skillful means of the various vehicles; he fully comprehends the benefit of those coming and going,
and having attained certainty, he emerges through the three vehicles and abides in the fruit of that single vehicle.
The nature of purity within the realm of all afflictions is able to utterly extinguish the fruits of all karma;
surpassing all rivers and oceans, it appears amidst the movement of tranquility,
casting away all afflictions, secondary afflictions, and their habitual tendencies.
By means of great compassion, wisdom, and skillful means, one abandons all conceptualizations regarding the benefit of sentient beings;
one also causes the cessation of the mind, consciousness,
and mentation that take all sentient beings as their objects, and thus understands the mentalities of all sentient beings.
In the minds of all sentient beings, In accordance with the intentions of all sentient beings,
Filling the hearts of all sentient beings, Causing the minds of all beings to rejoice,
Accomplishing the ultimate without error, May all erroneous understandings be abandoned.
Possessing the wisdom that is free from doubt regarding the three meanings—
the meaning of the five aggregates as the nature of the three kinds of qualities of the various selves throughout the three times— one is able to discern them within every moment;
thus, in a single moment, one attains perfect enlightenment and maintains the nature of all-encompassing awakening.
The bodyless body, supreme among bodies, which understands the limits of all bodies and manifests in various signs and locations;
this Great Jewel is the head of the Great Jewel.
Here follow fifteen verses.
This praises the Wisdom of Accomplishing What is to be Done (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*).
Thus, it manifests as the Buddha of the Accomplishment of Meaning (*arthasiddhi*) within the maṇḍala,
which consists of ninety-five names and numbers.
The one who understands all is the Perfectly Awakened One;
the awakening of perfect enlightenment is the unsurpassed, secret mantra source that is without letters.
The Great Secret Mantra is that which causes the three types of secret mantra meanings to increase; the Great Illuminating Bindu is without letters.
Great emptiness is the five syllables; the empty bindu is the sixth syllable.
The various kinds of emptiness are themselves devoid of variety;
the sixteen, each halved and endowed with a bindu, are likewise without parts, transcending all number. This is the very beginning of the four dhyānas.
Understanding all the factors of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-aṅga*), Clearly comprehending the nature of the lineages of meditative concentration,
Possessing the body of meditative concentration, supreme among bodies; The Enjoyment Body (*saṃbhogakāya*) is supreme over all,
And the Emanation Body (*nirmāṇakāya*) is the most excellent body, Which maintains the lineage of those emanations.
Manifesting in various forms throughout the ten directions, He benefits sentient beings according to the Dharma;
The Sovereign of Sovereigns, the God among Gods, Not a non-god, the Sovereign of Sovereigns, the Lord of Sovereigns,
The Teacher of the Unceasing Gods, The Maker and Destroyer— He is indeed the Sovereign.
He who brings about the transcendence of the tranquility of the three realms of existence, The sole Teacher, the Teacher of sentient beings,
whose fame pervades the ten directions; The Lord of Dharma, the Great One,
fully adorned with the armor of compassion, Who has made the mind of loving-kindness his firm mail.
Wisdom is like a sword; holding bow and arrow, one who seeks liberation can subdue the enemy of ignorance and the valiant Māra-foe.
Furthermore, one removes the four kinds of fearful Māras and can repel the armies of all Māras, attaining ultimate perfect enlightenment to save the world.
He is worthy of offerings, praise, and prostration; he is the constant object of service.
He is the most supreme field for veneration and hymns of praise, a sublime master truly worthy of homage.
With a single step, he can traverse the three worlds; like space, he is boundless and truly all-pervading.
Pure and possessing the three vidyās, you are pure; Endowed with the six superknowledges, you follow the six types of bodhisattvas, O great hero among heroes;
Possessing great supernormal powers, you transcend the world and have realized the true nature of that wisdom; You have also attained the very essence of wisdom.
Self-illuminating and illuminating others, this supreme being transcends all things and is beyond every analogy;
the Lord of the Victorious Ones, the Master of Wisdom and the Knowable,
is the Noble One who bestows the Dharma and proclaims the meaning of the four mudrās.
To the Supreme Lord to whom sentient beings offer gifts,
Within the subtle meaning of the three definitive abodes, pure and auspicious;
Possessing the great merit that accomplishes all auspiciousness within the three worlds, Mañjuśrī, the Victorious Auspiciousness.
The following five verses sequentially conclude the praise of the five wisdoms:
the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom, the Pure Dharma-Domain Wisdom, the Wondrous Observation Wisdom, the Equality Wisdom, and the All-Accomplishing Wisdom.
Each verse corresponds respectively to one wisdom.
I pay homage to the Victorious Giver of Vajras; I pay homage to the Ultimate Reality;
I pay homage to the Manifestation of Emptiness; I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened Bodhi.
I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who is attached; I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who desires;
I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who rejoices; I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who engages in conceptual play;
I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who smiles; I pay homage to the Perfectly Awakened One who laughs.
I pay homage to the speech of the Perfectly Awakened One; I pay homage to the mind of the Perfectly Awakened One;
I pay homage to that which appears without existence; I pay homage to the appearance of the Perfectly Awakened One;
I pay homage to the appearance of space; I pay homage to the appearance of wisdom.
I pay homage to the Net of Illusory Transformations; I pay homage to the Manifestation of Perfect Awakening;
I pay homage to all and everything; I pay homage to that Wisdom Body, Vajrapāṇi, the Holder of the Vajra.
This is the uncommon, true name of the Wisdom Hero Mañjuśrī;
it is the wisdom-body of the Bhagavān and the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas.
You should now give rise to great joy.
When the pure intention is fulfilled and increased to the unsurpassed state,
one is then able to purify the three secrets of body, speech, and mind;
if one cannot reach the ultimate, one will not be able to purify the stages (*bhūmi*).
May they reach the other shore, with both merit and wisdom fully perfected and purified;
may their realization be unsurpassed,
and should there be any who do not yet understand, may they come to understand.
I shall cause those who have not yet attained it to attain it;
from this point until the subtle and profound principles of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas are truly upheld,
I shall proclaim, reveal, elucidate, and explain them so that they may be fully embraced.
Vajrapāṇi, Holder of the Vajra:
I [entrust you] within your lineage and within the encompassment of the dharmatā of all secret mantras.
And he performs the act of gathering [beings],
namely Vajrapāṇi, the Holder of the Vajra;
this is the True Name.
This is the most utterly pure,
truly immaculate nature of the omniscient wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
it is the secret of the three— body, speech, and mind.
It is also the bodhi of all perfectly awakened ones (samyaksaṃbuddha),
for it is that which enables one to understand the true and ultimate state of all perfectly awakened ones.
It is also the unsurpassed state of all Tathāgatas.
He has realized the dharma-realm of all Sugatas;
among all victors, he is able to destroy the power of all Māras.
Among all those who possess the ten powers, he is the ten powers of the ten powers.
Within the nature of the knowledge of all-knowledge, there is the very nature of the knowledge of all-knowledge.
This is the decree among all phenomena;
it truly accomplishes all perfect enlightenment.
It is also the ultimate, stainless, and most perfectly pure fulfillment of both merit and wisdom for all great bodhisattvas.
It is also the source from which all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas arise.
It fully possesses the realms of humans and devas;
it is the essential nature of the Mahāyāna,
giving birth to the spheres of practice of all bodhisattvas.
It is the very limit of all noble paths;
it is also the place where the definitive emergence of all paths to liberation is discerned and measured;
and it is the uninterrupted lineage of the Tathāgatas.
It increases the lineage and family of the Bodhisattvas and Mahāsattvas,
and is also able to subdue all other mad enemies and destroy all non-Buddhists.
It is the relinquishing of the power of the four demonic generals;
it is also the true gathering-in of all sentient beings and the certain maturation of all who are directed toward the fruits of sainthood.
The meditations of the pure Brahma-heavens are the dhyānas of single-minded concentration;
they are also the subduing of the three— body, speech, and mind.
Through diligent application to meditative concentration, one is able to leave behind all conditioned aggregations,
relinquish all afflictions and secondary afflictions,
and eliminate all obstacles.
It liberates one from all fetters;
it is also liberation from all aggregates (*skandha*);
it extinguishes all distracted minds and brings fulfillment in every place of birth.
It abandons all matters of prosperity and decline,
and is also able to close the gates of all evil realms while revealing the supreme path of liberation and manifold bliss.
Causing them not to enter into saṃsāra,
yet enabling them to turn the great wheel of Dharma and establish the parasols, banners, and flags of all Tathāgatas.
It is the palace of all sublime and true dharmas;
it is also where bodhisattvas who practice through the gateway of secret mantras swiftly attain accomplishment.
This is also the understanding of the meditative concentration of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s diligent application to the perfection of wisdom;
it is the understanding of the emptiness of all diligent application, which is non-dual and free from conceptual proliferation.
The two-footed ones who have all reached the further shore;
those who have attained the ultimate, true, and pure state of all final stages;
and those who individually comprehend the Four Noble Truths of the sages.
With single-mindedness, one realizes all phenomena through the four foundations of mindfulness.
This true name [of the Buddha] encompasses,
up to and including, all the merits of perfect enlightenment.
It is capable of bringing about true and ultimate accomplishment.
O Vajrapāṇi, Holder of the Vajra,
this is the *Nāmasaṃgīti*.
It can extinguish, without remainder, the three types of karmic actions— of body, speech, and mind—
committed by sentient beings; it can also purify all the various classes of evil destinies for all sentient beings,
causing them to retreat from and abandon all such evil destinies.
It truly eliminates all karmic obstructions without exception;
it prevents the arising of the eight difficult conditions within any continuum of existence and extinguishes the eight kinds of fear.
It can destroy all evil dreams;
it is certain to exhaust all evil omens;
and it can extinguish all evil views as well as all malevolent māras.
It can also distance one from all the activities of hostile māras;
it increases all merit and goodness;
and it can eliminate all evil thoughts and reflections so that they do not arise.
It destroys all arrogance, prowess, and ego-clinging;
it gives rise to no suffering, affliction, or sorrow;
and it is also the heart-mind of all Tathāgatas.
The secret of all bodhisattvas;
the great secret of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
and all secret mantras and their mudrās.
Truly increasing ineffable mindfulness and right mindfulness,
they increase unsurpassed skillful wisdom,
and are also able to fulfill the powers and masteries that are free from affliction.
It can also increase auspiciousness, gentleness, goodness, and subtlety;
it brings forth renown, eloquent verses, praise, and beauty;
and it can truly eliminate all illnesses and vast terrors.
It is also the most utterly pure among all that is pure;
it is the most capable of producing purity among all that is capable of producing purity;
it is the most perfectly accomplished among all that is accomplished.
The most auspicious among the most auspicious;
he acts as a refuge for those who wish to take refuge,
and acts as a palace for those who desire a palace.
To those who wish for protection, he provides protection;
to those who wish for a general, he provides a general;
to those who wish for an island, he provides an island.
For those who wish to rely upon it, it serves as the unsurpassed reliance;
for those who wish to cross the great ocean of the three realms of existence, it serves as a boat;
and it is also the King of Medicines that eradicates all suffering of illness.
The decisive wisdom that discriminates between what is to be adopted and what is to be rejected;
the brilliant wisdom that destroys the great darkness of all evil views;
that which can fulfill the vows and aspirations of all sentient beings.
Like a maṇi jewel,
one may also attain the nature of the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī and the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna),
thereby enabling the five eyes to perceive pure wisdom.
Furthermore, because it is the true relinquishment of the three gifts— material gifts, the gift of Dharma, and the gift of fearlessness—
it causes the six perfections to reach fulfillment;
it is also the two bases of merit and wisdom, as well as all meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*).
Because it brings about ultimate consummation, one is able to attain the ten stages (*bhūmi*).
Furthermore, because one is able to abandon the two extremes,
this non-dual dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) is not any other kind of dharma-nature.
Because it is free from artifice and ornament, it is the nature of reality itself;
and because it is the nature of the Tathāgata’s pure wisdom,
it is the nature of the ultimate limit of reality.
Furthermore, because it can eliminate the dense forests of hundreds of thousands of evil views,
this True Name is the very nature of the true emptiness of all Tathāgatas.
This is the true name for the meaning of the non-dual nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
For anyone who recites, upholds, or expounds it,
this is the ineffable intrinsic nature of all phenomena.
Vajrapāṇi, the Vajra-holder:
if there are sons or daughters of good family who practice according to the gateway of secret mantras.
This is the *Tathāgataguhyasamāja-nāma-mañjuśrījñānasattvasarvatathāgatajñānakāyādvaya-tattvanāma-uṣṇīṣa-tilaka*,
the true name of the wisdom-being Mañjuśrī, the Blessed One, which is the single essence of the non-dual suchness of the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas.
It is the jewel upon the crown.
One thoroughly penetrates all the meanings of the words and phrases;
there is nothing omitted or transgressed, nor anything added or diminished.
Three times each day, one should either uphold, recite, read, or explain them.
Contemplating the meaning and principles, one should explain them to others according to the occasion;
at each such time, one should visualize the body of Mañjuśrī, the Wisdom Hero,
and cause the mind to rest within the various gateways.
Within the gateway of the true nature of what is cherished, one forms thoughts with sincerity;
possessing wisdom that understands all sublime dharmas without turbidity,
and endowed with faith, one maintains a continuous stream of mindfulness and single-minded meditative concentration.
All those who have attained perfect awakening throughout the three times and the beginningless past,
including all bodhisattvas and vidyādharas, gathered together;
they attained the realization of all phenomena and manifested their own bodies.
All the Bodhisattvas of Perfect Awakening,
through the three karmas of body, speech, and mind, truly embrace me with their own seed-nature.
All the Bodhisattvas of Perfect Awakening.
They shall bring about benefit and provide assistance for all;
they shall attain fearlessness and unimpeded eloquence in the exposition of all dharmas;
furthermore, they shall be sustained by all the arhats, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
Within the minds of the noble ones, these deities also manifest their forms.
Furthermore, there are the Great Vajra Kings who subdue all evils, such as Mahāvajradhara and others,
who appear for the sake of protecting all sentient beings.
He manifests various forms through his transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*), such that no one can subdue his spiritual power or majesty;
he is able to accomplish all secret mantras, mudrās, signs, and maṇḍalas without exception.
The King of Secret Mantras and Vidyā-mantras,
together with Vināyakas and all malevolent māras and adversaries,
as well as all those who cause ruin and destruction, those who cannot be overcome by others, the Mātṛkās, and so forth.
At every moment of every day and night,
throughout all modes of conduct, they remain hidden within his body to provide protection;
furthermore, there are the Pure Brahmās, Śakra, and Śakra’s close ministers.
With great power he subdues them as one would a mere infant;
likewise Mahādeva, the Cat-like offspring of the lineage, Mahākāla, Līlāvatī,
Yama the Lord of Hells, and Varuṇa the Water God.
The *Kumbhāṇḍas* such as Pukkasi and the Mother of Demons,
who protect the worlds of the ten directions, shall constantly and continuously provide guardianship,
whether by day or by night, whether walking or standing still.
Whether sitting, lying down, sleeping, or awake;
whether entering or emerging from meditative concentration;
whether dwelling alone or in a crowd—[the Buddha] remains hidden within his body to provide protection.
Or they may dwell in villages, towns, settlements, riverbanks, plains,
national borders, royal palaces, thresholds, gate towers, great roads,
narrow paths, crossroads, or triple junctions.
Villages, shops, empty houses,
mountains, thickets, rivers, streams, groves, and great forests—
any place where one might become intoxicated, heedless, or negligent, unless it has been purified.
Constantly, throughout all gates, day and night, they remain hidden, providing supreme protection and accomplishing sublime bliss.
Furthermore, there are devas, nāgas, obstructors, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the various luminaries that wander and lodge therein.
Together with the various Devamātṛs, the Gaṇādhipas, the Seven Mothers, the Balarāmas, the Piśācīs, and the Māṃsādas—
all these assembled with one heart and one mind,
along with their army generals, retinues, and various messengers.
It is able to provide secret protection for all,
increasing the spirit and endowing one with physical strength and vitality;
its majestic power is preeminent, bringing freedom from illness and longevity.
Vajrapāṇi, the Vajra-holder:
if one makes this vow regarding this *Uṣṇīṣa-maṇi*,
the *Nāmasaṃgīti*, three times each day;
Recite this without omission three times, write it down, and have it read.
At that time, one should perform meditative concentration while visualizing oneself as the body of the Bhagavān Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, exactly as described here.
Because of this benefit, before long,
Mañjuśrī manifested a transformed image so that he might see it,
and he also saw those who dwell throughout the entirety of the realm of space.
O Bodhisattva of All-Perfect Awakening,
at what time and by means of what activity do you manifest as these various bodily forms for the sake of great sentient beings?
They shall not fall into the realm of hell nor be born in the evil destinies;
they shall not be born into low-caste families or as outcasts in remote regions,
but shall possess all their faculties in full and refrain from holding wrong views.
Furthermore, they will not be born into families with wrong views, nor will they be born in lands where no Buddha dwells.
When they are born in a land where a Buddha resides, they will not abandon the True Dharma, nor will they distance themselves from it.
They will not be born among the long-lived gods of the heavens, nor will they be born during kalpas of famine, pestilence, or warfare.
They shall not be born in the five turbidities of an evil age, nor shall they encounter the fear of kings, the fear of evil men, or the fear of thieves.
Throughout their successive lives, they shall not meet with the fear of inferiority or poverty.
They shall not encounter the terrors of foul odors, slander, contempt, ill repute, or harsh speech.
They will constantly be born into naturally noble and eminent lineages;
they will possess all the marks of physical excellence and a beautiful complexion,
becoming objects of affection and delight for all people in the world.
If he accompanies others, his disposition is harmonious and joyful, bringing delight to those who behold him.
Among all people, he is upright and handsome,
endowed with the marks of great merit, and his speech is unhindered.
In whatever place they are born, they attain the knowledge of past lives;
they enjoy vast abundance and many followers;
their enjoyments are inexhaustible and their retinue is inexhaustible.
He is the most preeminent among all sentient beings and is likewise endowed with supreme functional power;
he naturally possesses the six pāramitās.
All meritorious qualities abide within the four palaces of the pure Brahmā realm,
being fully endowed with mindfulness, right mindfulness, skillful means, the power of aspiration, and wisdom;
they are likewise present within all numerical categories and meanings.
They attain fearlessness and the ability to speak;
free from delusion, they clarify every word and phrase,
becoming greatly wise and possessing extensive understanding.
Free from indolence, possessing few desires and being content,
one benefits others extensively while remaining free from attachment;
this is the ground of supreme trust for all sentient beings.
They also achieve reverence for their teachers and preceptors.
Regarding all previously unheard teachings on crafts, arts, and supernormal powers—
whether in terms of their words or their meaning— they will fully comprehend them all.
The precepts and the livelihood are the most supreme among all practices; they are the most supremely pure and subtle,
pertaining to renunciation and the attainment of full ordination.
He shall not cause one to forget or lose the great bodhicitta, which is the nature of the knowledge of all modes;
he shall certainly not enter the vehicles of the śrāvakas, arhats, or pratyekabuddhas.
O Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi!
Thus he is endowed with immeasurable merit,
and likewise possesses such immeasurable, boundless, and vast merit,
O Vajrapāṇi, Holder of the Vajra.
One who recites this *Tathāgatasya nāma-saṃgīti* is one who truly upholds the subtle and wondrous Great Being;
such a person gathers and becomes fully endowed with subtle and wondrous merit and wisdom.
Because one seeks the supreme qualities of all perfectly awakened ones with extreme swiftness,
one is able to accomplish true, ultimate, and unsurpassed bodhi without passing much time.
Throughout many eons, they do not enter nirvana,
but extensively manifest the unsurpassed, wondrous Dharma for all sentient beings,
expounding and elucidating that wondrous Dharma throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
The sound of the great drum continues without ceasing;
its roar proclaims him as the Great Dharma King.
Furthermore, Śrīvajradhara, with a heart full of joy, joins his palms in reverence.

Having paid homage to the Tathāgata, the Venerable Bhagavān, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Venerable Guhyasvabhāva then addressed the Vajradhara, the King of Vajras, and all the other various co-dwellers in these words with a loud voice:
[Note: The Tibetan text provided corresponds to the opening of the *Guhyasamāja-tantra*. The Sanskrit reconstruction for the verse is:
tathāgatam bhagavantam vande 'haṃ samyaksambuddham atyantam | punar api guhyasvabhāvo vajradharo vajrarājā ca || anye ca ye vividhāḥ sahasthāyinas tatraiva | uccaiḥ svareṇaivam āmantrayām āsa ||
Venerable One, we too rejoice; well said, well said—how excellent!
For those sentient beings who seek the fruit of liberation and are without a protector, may we become their true saviors and bring about the great benefit of protecting them on the path to Bodhi.
The subtle principle of illusory manifestation has been proclaimed; this is the pure and subtle path, profound and most vast.
It is that which brings benefit to sentient beings of great purpose and constitutes the sphere of all the Perfectly Awakened Ones—all the Perfectly Awakened Ones have already taught it.
The Bhagavān Mañjuśrījñānasattva has finished reciting the *Tathatā-nāma-saṃgīti*,
as spoken by the Bhagavān, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
The true teaching of all Buddhas of the three times, The true king among all secrets—
This *Mañjuśrī-nāma-saṃgīti* has been translated with truth and without partiality,
For the sake of protecting true roots of virtue, So that all sentient beings may become truly [awakened].
Truly severing all afflictions, Swiftly attaining the state of a truly ultimate Buddha;
Truly not understanding worldly dialects, Yet truly expressing words with eloquence—
To Mañjuśrī, whose true name is sublime, And who possesses inconceivable, true virtues.
Seeing the benefit of reality, abandon what is right and wrong; according to one's capacity, rectify through reality those passages where the meaning is inverted or lost.
May the wise restore the truth and correct it.
This was composed by the Official for the Evaluation of Monks, a Śramaṇa, who originally lectured on the Sūtras, Vinaya, and Abhidharma, and whose merit lay in his renunciation.

This is the *Praise of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Mañjuśrī*.
Translated by the Master Zhìhuì, a nephew of the Master Fēnzhēn, who was the Prefectural Magistrate of Shānmǎtí Mountain at Gānquán.
With the most supremely pure and true mind, I perpetually prostrate at the crown of the head of the Most Honored One.
All Buddhas together give this instruction: I shall now proclaim the various names of Mañjuśrī.
His body is of wondrous color and marks, upright and majestic; among all forms, it is the most honored.
He fully understands all the primary and secondary marks; Mañjuśrī’s valor is the ultimate reality.
Possessing inconceivable thought and the severance [of delusion], it is the source from which vast arts and skills emerge.
The three bodies (trikāya) penetrate the inconceivable; such a mental capacity is inconceivable.
Through the power of concentration on emptiness, it is spontaneous. Emptiness is the reality that possesses the true Dharma.
The nature of emptiness is the supreme joy; the phenomena of the three realms of existence are shown to be empty.

Contemplating the state of universal liberation, he is the sovereign of all classes, both self and other, the most honored among the multitudes of all sentient beings—to him, all sentient beings pay homage.
So it is with all those in the five realms of existence;
All malevolent spirits, māras, and hostile enemies are utterly destroyed. The Honored One among men roars the lion’s roar;
his afflictions are softened, he is free from all evils, And all obstacles, defilements, and stains are completely removed.
All sentient beings come to protect him; thus liberated from the nine realms of existence, he possesses the *mudrā* and has long, flowing hair.
Dwelling within the pure palace of Brahmā, he holds a rosary in his hand and carries a staff;
he is the accumulation of skillful means who is both pure and impure.
Mañjuśrī of beautiful voice is ever the Lord; The lotus-born one with golden-colored lotus roots is most excellent.
Seated upon a vast lotus throne, holding pure maṇḍārava flowers, He dwells auspiciously and well, endowed with a sublime mind.
He is the Perfectly Awakened One and the Solitary Realizer;
he is one who has already attained Buddhahood in previous lives, possessing mastery over supernatural powers.
He is the Teacher of the Four Noble Truths, the Thousand-Eyed Protector of the World, and the Lord of the Nine Abodes endowed with wisdom.
He is the honored one among all beings, each and every one; he is the most supreme among all classes of beings.
He is the honored king of beasts from whom all are born; thus possessing power, he takes pity on the world and subdues all classes of beings through skillful eloquence.
Such a son of the Buddha is a Buddha, a true Buddha.
His body is as brilliantly radiant as a thousand suns; He is also the full moon, the lord of the stars’ splendor;
He is also the prince of the water-gods and the great sovereign king Maheśvara;
He is also the various dragon kings of Sāgara; And he is the master of all the aggregates.
Lord of the Earth, Śrīśubhaṃkara; Honored One to whom the valiant hosts of devas assemble;
Honored One to whom the gathered devas pay homage; Stainless Honored One among the guardians of the realm;
Most Honored One, supreme among those free from outflows in the world; Honored One of the world who understands worldly affairs.
Possessing that wisdom and understanding is the truth; through various deeds and practices, he provides protection such that the factions of evil Māras dare not touch him.
Fully comprehending the profound and subtle Dharma, the Dharma Master personally gathers these three matters;
like a king of physicians, he extracts the arrows of the three poisons.
All those difficult to subdue are thoroughly subdued; those endowed with wisdom are able to understand.
Possessing worldly power and capable of performing deeds, they are likewise the wish-fulfilling tree of merit and wisdom, adorned with the branches, leaves, and flowers of bodhi.
The fruit of liberation ripens, and the three things converge.
The Honored One who is the refuge for all classes of sentient beings;
The Honored One who enters the minds of beings, seizes their minds, and is free from defilement through the practice of Brahma-conduct;
He is also the Lord of the host of stellar deities, And the Great Sage, the Sovereign of patience; He is also the one in the final birth, endowed with the rank of a king.
He is also the Honored One of Equal Enlightenment on the Ten Stages;
he is the Lord of the Dharma who is honored within the Sangha, the most supreme Teacher, and the Master of Nirvāṇa.
He is also the Lord of space, earth, and water, as well as the Lord of the nature of fire and wind. He is also the true wish-fulfilling jewel.
I pay homage to all the Bhagavāns who fulfill the needs of sentient beings;
I pay homage to Mañjuśrī, who is like a precious jewel.
Having thus praised and described his marks and signs, one should receive this understanding and constantly recite and uphold it in the mind.
One who remains far removed from all evil karma And attains the fruit of supreme purity—
If a person constantly recites these one hundred and eight names and other titles at the three times of day,
Whatever arises in their mind will be fulfilled according to their wishes; Within a state of doubt-free mind, they shall realize them all.
Those who remember and uphold these sublime marks and signs will be purified of all immediate karmic offenses (*ānantarya*) and all impure evil deeds; all such things shall be utterly extinguished.
Even when approaching the end of life and departing for another realm, should any evil signs or adverse conditions appear, [they shall be overcome].
With a pure mind, constantly recollecting and upholding [this], one will personally behold the courageous Mañjuśrī.
Among those possessing wisdom, he is supremely pure; who can read, recite, and uphold this?
If one wishes to realize the fruit of Buddhahood, there is no doubt that it will be decisively realized within the mind.
In Sanskrit: *Āryamañjuśrīstuti*. In Chinese: *Shengzhe Wenshushili Zan* (Praise to the Holy Mañjuśrī).
Most exceptionally sublime among all gathered assemblies, Like the full moon that eclipses all other lights.
With ignorance and afflictions entirely purified, Mañjuśrī, I pay homage to you!
O Jvālākeśa, most brilliantly radiant, Your body is majestic with shimmering jewels, Your eyes are deep blue, and your form is a blazing flame; Mañjuśrī, I pay homage to you!
The nectar of a single flavor, profound and gentle; A voice that enters the heart, resonant and true—a treasure-trove of the wondrous Dharma.
Mañjuśrī, I pay homage to you in every place throughout the Sahā world. Who could measure the number of raindrops that fall?
Having completely cast off the defilements of the afflictions, I pay homage to Mañjuśrī.
Beholding the eyes and the physical form of Mañjuśrī, which are like a *mandārava* flower—never tiring of the sight—I offer all phenomena as a bowl of alms; I pay homage to Mañjuśrī.
To the Buddhas dwelling in the realms of the ten directions, Who with vast and sublime voices constantly praise the Supreme Teacher of sentient beings— Mañjuśrī, I pay homage to you;
O Noble Mañjuśrī, I offer my praise. May all the roots of virtue gathered through these acts Be dedicated to the welfare of all beings.
I offer all to the sentient beings of the entire Dharma-realm; May they swiftly realize the true path to Nirvāṇa.
I take refuge in the Imperial Net that transcends the three limits of time; May the inexhaustible Triple Gem look upon me with compassion.
O Seventh Patriarch, Great Holy Lord, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Look upon me with compassion.
Muni Ratnakūṭa, Lord of Great Compassion, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, look upon us with compassion!
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Sovereign Sage who attained fruition in a previous aeon, look upon us with compassion!
Lord Mañjughoṣa, Great Holy Sovereign, and the assembly of noble ones gathered like an ocean, look upon us with compassion!
May the obstacles caused by evil mental factors be removed; may I be guided along the path that accords with my wishes.

By this root of virtue, may I attain Buddhahood; having attained it, may I destroy all faults, enemies, and the sea of suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death, extensively delivering all sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra.
May those who have not yet reached the place where truth arises, And all Tathāgatas,

ultimate Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas, Obtain the sovereignty of a king who governs with leisure and mastery, Thoroughly cultivate the three trainings until they reach perfection, And constantly benefit others without ever regressing.
Free from the dust and defilements of phenomena, one attains firm stability;
at all places of enlightenment, one constantly and respectfully seeks to cultivate the sublime Dharma of excellent renown.
Its fragrance spreads far and wide throughout the ten directions, and when ultimate perfect awakening is attained, it is perpetually offered as an act of worship.
To those who can act as a refuge and protector, Who are humble, respectful, and endowed with virtue—
May I always draw near to such spiritual friends,
Whose merit is as firm as Mount Sumeru, And whose nature of wisdom shines like the light of the sun and moon.
May my fame spread far and wide like space; may these three things be constantly fulfilled.
May my life span extend for a hundred years and beyond a hundred autumns; may my enjoyment of health and prosperity increase.
May I certainly be born into the lineage of the Mahāyāna; may these five things be constantly fulfilled.
May all who harbor malice and come here—whether dwelling on the earth or in the air—always give rise to a heart of loving-kindness toward sentient beings.
Day and night, according to the proper time, may they practice the sublime Dharma;
seeing that all things in this world are like illusions and transformations, may they be able to relinquish what they receive, for even these are empty.
Thus, practicing generosity according to what is obtained, the perfection of generosity is fully realized;
Maintaining the precepts while remaining free from defilement, being endowed with purity and free from transgression,
and being detached from attachment to the precepts, the perfection of ethical discipline is fully realized.
This body is a composite of the four elements—earth, water, fire, and wind; its inherent nature is empty.
Though subjected to various harms, it remains free from anger. Thus, the perfection of patience is fully realized.
With boundless diligence, one practices with certainty; the defilements of laziness cannot invade.
With body and mind fully endowed with such power, the perfection of diligence is completely fulfilled.
With all meditative concentrations that are like illusions and transformations, and with the samādhis of courageous fearlessness,
the perfection of meditative concentration is completely fulfilled— like the vajra-like samādhi.
The three gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the realization of the true essence as a single flavor equal throughout the three times;
the suchness of all awakened ones’ principles; the perfection of the wisdom-pāramitās—all as taught by all Tathāgatas;
with blazing radiance and majestic spiritual power.
Through the power of the diligence of Bodhisattva Vīravīra, may all my aspirations now be fulfilled.
I take refuge in the auspicious and wise Vīravīra; he who elucidates the profound meaning of true suffering.
Now, by reciting this for the sake of all sentient beings, may we together attain the auspicious Vajra-wisdom.

[Symbol] [Symbol] [Symbol] [Symbol] [Symbol] Oṃ a hūṃ ha ra pa tsa na. The Five-Syllable Heart Mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva: A RA PA TSA NA. The *Vajraśekhara Sūtra* explains the supreme characteristics of this five-syllable mantra as follows: [text continues].
If a person recites it even once,
it is as if they have recited the eighty-four thousand twelve Veda-piṭaka sūtras;
if they recite it twice, [the merit is doubled].
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra follow and bestow their empowerment upon them;
the Dharma-protecting benevolent deities stand before such persons.
Furthermore, O son of good family or daughter of good family:
If there is one who can maintain this mantra and recite it even once,
they will immediately enter into the equality of all dharmas of the Tathāgata;
all letters, as well, are equal.
One will swiftly achieve the realization of Mahāprajñā.
Furthermore, reciting it even once can eliminate all hardships and calamities for the practitioner.
If one recites it twice,
the grave sins of birth and death accumulated over billions of kalpas will be extinguished;
if one recites it three times, samādhi will manifest before one.
If one recites it four times, one will not forget the dhāraṇī.
If one recites it five times, one will swiftly attain unsurpassed bodhi.
If a person dwells alone in a quiet and secluded place with a single-minded focus, they should [construct] a five-syllable wheel maṇḍala using Brahmi script.
Once one has completed a month of recitation according to the ritual,
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva will manifest his form,
or he will expound the essential points of the Dharma from within the sky.
At that time, the practitioner attains knowledge of past lives,
possesses unimpeded eloquence and mastery of the supernormal powers,
fulfills supreme vows, and becomes complete in merit and wisdom.
They will swiftly all realize the Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
by merely believing and accepting it with their minds,
they will attain perfect enlightenment after sixteen lifetimes.
The visualization method of the syllable *cakra* (wheel) was received from a teacher.
